_comment: Canonical cross-language SERIALIZATION-EQUIVALENCE corpus (LED-2 phase 2). Single source of truth: go encodes each vector ONCE with deterministic marshalling and the bytes are checked in below as `hex`; go, java, python, rust and typescript each decode THAT blob with their generated CorpusRecord type and assert the decoded values equal `expect` exactly. Regenerate `hex` after editing `expect` with `cross-test/wire-corpus/run.sh --emit` — never hand-edit an `expect` value to make a decoder agree; a disagreement is a real cross-language finding.

vectors.name: full
vectors._comment: Every covered shape populated. int64 at the negative boundary, uint64 above 2^53, a 3-entry map whose declaration order is NOT sorted order, `optional` PRESENT carrying its zero value, and non-UTF-8 bytes.

vectors.name: sparse
vectors._comment: The transpose. int64 at the positive boundary, uint64 at 2^64-1, no map entries, `optional` ABSENT, empty bytes. Distinguishing this vector from `full` on opt_count is only possible for a runtime that models proto3 explicit presence.
